knowledge_units.statement: Process-industry functional-safety practice assigns safe-state achievement and maintenance to a safety instrumented system, and safety integrity can be undermined when protection depends on the same basic process-control components whose failure creates the demand.
qualifiers: The IEC public page establishes the SIS lifecycle/safe-state role; the HSE notice supplies a concrete common-cause failure example and cites the relevant BS EN 61511 independence/dependency clauses.

knowledge_units.statement: A supervisory command layer can be added above an already stabilized lower-level controller and constrain the requested reference so that state/control bounds, actuator magnitude limits, actuator rate limits, and process-variable limits are respected.
qualifiers: Reference-governor theory assumes a pre-stabilized system; it does not by itself establish safety integrity for the supervisory computation.

knowledge_units.statement: Constrained MPC provides a second established framework for optimization under explicit hard state and control constraints rather than sending unconstrained optimizer outputs directly to the process.
qualifiers: Constraint satisfaction still depends on model adequacy, feasibility assumptions, implementation, and the target process; the evidence does not provide universal numerical bounds.

knowledge_units.statement: A directly relevant industrial implementation keeps conventional PID loops, PLC logic, and safety interlocks at Level 1 while a Level 2 MPC layer changes only temperature setpoints subject to process constraints.
qualifiers: This is one continuous-steel-annealing implementation and should be treated as an architecture example, not as proof that the same controller hierarchy is sufficient for every process.

knowledge_units.statement: The same industrial implementation preserves operation when supervisory MPC is disconnected by reverting to operator-set Level 1 setpoints, and introduced automatic operation gradually through progressively longer trials.
qualifiers: The evidence establishes fallback/manual operation and staged commissioning, but does not prescribe a universal hold-last, automatic fallback, or bumpless-transfer policy.

knowledge_units.statement: Taken together, the evidence supports a layered architecture in which the optimization/prediction layer is supervisory, constraint enforcement occurs before lower-level setpoint application, the established lower-level regulatory controller remains responsible for fast closed-loop regulation, and independent safety protection remains available when the supervisory layer fails or is disconnected.
qualifiers: This is a cross-source engineering synthesis. Exact layer boundaries, safety-function allocation, fallback state, watchdog behavior, and communication semantics require target-process hazard and control analysis.

relations.description: The layered supervisory architecture is safety-credible only if failure or loss of the supervisory/BPCS path does not also remove the safety function.
Reference-governor and constrained-MPC literature independently support explicit constraint enforcement at the command/optimization boundary.
The control-theory mechanisms for constrained commands are consistent with the industrial pattern of a supervisory optimizer writing bounded setpoints to a lower-level PLC/PID layer.
Operational robustness of the supervisory architecture depends not only on normal automatic operation but also on a defined fallback path and controlled commissioning.

uncertainties.description: The selected evidence does not determine target-process numerical limits for setpoint magnitude, setpoint rate, optimizer update interval, state constraints, or acceptable settling/oscillation metrics.
The Tata Steel implementation is a single continuous-process example, so its exact Level 1/Level 2 decomposition and operational practices are not universal requirements.
The selected evidence does not specify a universal PLC communication watchdog, timeout action, hold-last policy, bumpless-transfer design, or safe fallback setpoint for the user's target process.
